key_insight: Mesh4D encodes an entire dynamic object's animation from a monocular video into a single compact latent vector so a feed-forward decoder can reconstruct a temporally coherent 4D mesh (shape + motion) in one pass. A skeletal-guided autoencoder injects strong priors for plausible deformations.
problem_solved: Reconstructing complete, temporally consistent 3D shape and per-frame motion (4D mesh) of a dynamic object from a single monocular video stream without expensive per-sequence optimization or multi-view input.
method: Train an autoencoder to learn a compact latent space that represents an entire animation sequence; during training the latent space is constrained by the object's skeletal structure to encode realistic deformations.
Use a feed-forward decoder that, given the sequence latent code, outputs a deformation field and per-frame meshes to reconstruct full 3D geometry and motion.
At inference, encode a monocular video into one latent code and decode it in a single pass to produce temporally consistent 4D meshes and tracked topology.
impact: Enables fast, scalable monocular 4D reconstruction and tracking for applications like animation, AR/VR, and video analysis, removing the need for per-sequence optimization and improving temporal coherence of reconstructed meshes.

paper_title: Mesh4D: 4D Mesh Reconstruction and Tracking from Monocular Video
paper_authors: Zeren Jiang, Chuanxia Zheng, Iro Laina, Diane Larlus, Andrea Vedaldi
